questions.question: Which command is used to delete a variable in ObjectScript?
questions.explanation: KILL x deletes the variable entirely. SET x = "" only assigns an empty string — the variable still exists.

questions.question: What does the following code print?
questions.explanation: $PIECE(str, ",", 2) returns the 2nd piece delimited by , → World.

questions.question: What does $ORDER(arr("")) return?

options.text: The value of the first element in the array
The first key in the array
The total number of elements in the array

questions.explanation: $ORDER(arr("")) returns the first key in the array, not its value.

questions.question: What does the following code print?
$DATA(arr(5)) returns 10. What does this mean?

options.text: Node arr(5) has data and has children
Node arr(5) has no data but has children
Node arr(5) has data but no children

questions.explanation: $DATA = 10 means the node has no data value itself, but has descendant subscripts (children).

questions.question: What does the following code print?
To pass a multidimensional array into a method, what must you do?

options.text: Declare ByRef in the signature and call with . before the variable
Use MERGE to copy the array before passing it
ObjectScript does not support passing arrays into methods

questions.explanation: Declare ByRef pArr in the method signature and call with ..Method(.myArray).

questions.question: What does the following code print?
questions.explanation: $TRANSLATE(str, "ace") with no third argument deletes all occurrences of a, c, e → bd.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly retrieves the last element of a $LIST?

options.text: Both A and B are valid

questions.explanation: Both are valid: $LG(list, $LL(list)) (by index) and $LG(list, -1) (negative index from end).

questions.question: What is wrong with the following code?

options.text: Missing %Status check — if %Save() fails, the error is silently ignored
Must use DO instead of SET when calling %Save()

questions.explanation: Always check $$$ISERR(sc) after %Save() — failing silently is a common mistake in IRIS development.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to iterate over all elements of a $LIST? (select all that apply)

options.text: SET p=0  WHILE $LISTNEXT(list, p, val) { WRITE val, ! }
SET key=""  FOR { SET key=$ORDER(list(key))  QUIT:key=""  WRITE list(key),! }

questions.explanation: FOR i=1:1:$LL and $LISTNEXT are the two correct ways. C uses global-style $ORDER which doesn't work on $LIST. D uses zero-based bracket syntax which is invalid in ObjectScript.
